Eli (Product): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can folks help me distill our short pitch vs cloud-managed endpoints and vs self-hosted inference vendors? Need a 1-2 line answer to put in the S&M one-pager.
Sam (CEO): Short version: we sell predictable inference outcomes — not just model access. Focus on latency, cost predictability, and operational controls across hosted, dedicated, and private.
Maya (CTO): Tech angle: our runtime + smart routing + caching reduces per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs. That’s different from a model-serving endpoint that treats each request independently.
Ren (Eng): Also add: unified rollout & observability — same API, same tracing, same canary policies whether you're on hosted or on-prem. Makes ops cheaper.
Anya (Sales): Helpful. For customers asking about "vendor lock-in" vs self-hosted, what's the concise answer?
Sam (CEO): We enable portability — customers can start on hosted, move to Dedicated or Private with the same API and operational model. Not an instant swap sometimes, but it’s the same semantics.
Maya (CTO): Practically: we version models and config so rollouts are consistent. Private includes control-plane adapters so infra differences are limited.
Ren (Eng): From an infra POV: we provide migration guides + data plane binaries; some infra work is always needed on-prem but we try to minimize config drift.
Eli (Product): How do we position vs cloud AI: "use cloud for model diversity and scale, use Redwood for production economics"?
Sam (CEO): Yeah — cloud AI == fast access to models. Redwood == predictable unit economics and SLOs at scale. Emphasize SLAs, observability, and cost-controls.
Anya (Sales): Customers ask about price comparisons — any thumb rules (hosted vs dedicated)?
Maya (CTO): Short rule: for bursty, low-volume workloads hosted is cheaper/time-to-value. For steady high-throughput (sustained tokens/hour) Dedicated or Private wins on $/token due to reserved capacity and optimized kernels.
Ren (Eng): Add: model quantization + batching profiles we recommend can shave 30–60% cost depending on workload. Mention that as a lever.
Eli (Product): Competitors: do we call out managed cloud endpoints explicitly or keep it generic?
Sam (CEO): Keep it product-focused in outward doc: "managed endpoints" and "inference infra vendors". Internally we can map to specific competitors but public marketing should be about outcomes.
Anya (Sales): Noted — I'll add bullets to the playbook. Who owns the short 2-line pitch?
Sam (CEO): Eli, draft one pager. Maya, Ren — add 1–2 tech bullets. Anya — I'll loop you for GTM language. OpsBot: Meeting recording uploaded: https://redwood.company/records/all-hands/1847501234 :movie_camera:
Eli (Product): Thanks all — I'll post a draft in #product for feedback and a sales-ready blurb in #sales by EOD. :thumbsup:
Maya (CTO): +1, will add kernel/quant notes to the doc.
Ren (Eng): Ping me if you need numbers for cost examples.
Anya (Sales): Will do. Thanks!
